methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i lesson.mp4 -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -f f4v lesson.f4v.
methods.limits: Composed documented encoding syntax; local F4V muxer and H.264/AAC encoders required.

methods.steps: For compatible H.264/AAC input, run ffmpeg -i compatible.mp4 -c copy -f f4v compatible.f4v.
methods.limits: Only suitable tracks can be copied; this is a different workflow from the site transcode.
Explicit M2TS mode; stream compatibility and automatic selection must be reviewed.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i delivery.mp4 -c:v libx264 -c:a ac3 -mpegts_m2ts_mode 1 delivery.m2ts.
methods.limits: Creates new lossy video/audio; not equivalent to site stream copying or guaranteed disc compliance.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i exhibit.mp4 -c:v rv10 -b:v 800k -c:a ac3 exhibit.rm.
methods.limits: Requires RV10/AC-3 encoder support and a player accepting this combination; composed documented syntax.
Intentionally discards all sound; local RV20 encoder and receiving-player support required.

methods.steps: Run ffmpeg -i seminar.mpeg -c:a wmav2 -b:v 1200k -c:v wmv2 seminar.wmv.
methods.limits: Names WMV2 video and WMA v2 audio; local encoders required.
NEF is read-only and PDF readable and writable in the formats list; PDF output requires Ghostscript.
ORF is read-only and JPEG readable and writable in the formats list.
ORF is read-only and PNG readable and writable in the formats list; PNG output requires libpng.
PBM and PNG are both readable and writable in the formats list.

methods.steps: In Python, run from PIL import Image, then Image.open("mask.pbm").save("mask.png").
methods.limits: Pillow reads plain and raw PBM and takes the output format from the file ending.
PCX and JPEG are both readable and writable in the formats list.

methods.steps: In Python, run from PIL import Image, then Image.open("clipart.pcx").convert("RGB").save("clipart.jpg").
methods.limits: convert("RGB") turns a palette image into RGB before the JPEG is written.
PES is read-only and JPEG readable and writable in the formats list.

methods.steps: Open the PES with File > Open in Inkscape, then use File > Save a copy and pick PNG; save a JPG from that PNG in an image editor.
methods.limits: Ink/Stitch must be installed in Inkscape; PNG is one of its utility output formats.
